title: Session-level keepalive & salvage protocol for disconnected streaming clients
creator: Arianna Patel
description: Problem: Client disconnects and network blips lead to orphaned/incomplete streaming generations. Current heuristics evict partial outputs aggressively which causes user-visible regressions and extra cost on retries. We need a deterministic, session-scoped keepalive + salvage (resume/token reconciliation) protocol that: 1) preserves partial outputs where safe, 2) prevents resource starvation under backpressure, 3) interoperates with older SDKs that don't support resume tokens, and 4) maintains SLOs for tail latency and resource efficiency. This ticket designs and implements server-side session keepalive, salvage rules for partial KV cache reuse, and a compatibility fallback for legacy clients.
acceptance_criteria: Server exposes a session_id on stream open and returns short-lived resume_token after first meaningful delta
A keepalive window (configurable, default 45s) prevents immediate discard of partial generations on transient disconnects
If client reconnects with a valid resume_token within the keepalive window, generation resumes without rerunning full forward pass and final output merges deterministically
Legacy clients (no resume_token support) are handled by a conservative grace window before eviction; metrics show <2% increase in memory retention under typical load
Integration tests cover: normal stream, disconnect+resume, disconnect+exceed-grace->evict, simultaneous reconnect attempts, and tool-calling handshake during resume
Benchmarks demonstrate no degradation in 95th percentile latency beyond 5% under peak throughput with salvage enabled
technical_notes: Session lifecycle: stream_open -> session_id issued (UUID v4) -> server allocates ephemeral session record with last_active timestamp and reference to KV cache shards
Resume token: opaque HMAC(token_payload) that encodes session_id, model_version, sequence_offset, and cache_shard_ids. Signed for tamper resistance and short TTL (default 2 min).

Keepalive policy: server accepts either explicit keepalive ping from client or inferred keepalive via background heartbeat on active route. If gap > keepalive_window -> session marked orphaned and enters salvage queue.

Salvage workflow: enqueue partial session for quick resume window (keepalive_window). During salvage, allow cached KV reuse only if model_variant and quantization profile match; otherwise serve fallback full generation with graceful merge and annotation in structured output indicating partial merge.

Backpressure integration: session records count toward memory caps. When memory budget is tight, evict oldest orphaned sessions preferentially based on cost heuristic (tokens_generated * model_compute_cost).

Compatibility: SDK v1.0 clients (legacy) do not send resume_token. For these, we provide a short conservational grace (default 10s) and emit a structured 'session_unavailable' event on reconnect so apps can decide to retry with fresh prompt. Recommend SDK bump to v1.2 for resume support.

Tool/function-calling considerations: if a partially completed generation had already invoked an external tool (e.g., code-exec or search), ensure idempotency: record tool-call id in session record and on resume, suppress duplicate calls or mark duplicates as 'replayed' in structured output. Requires instrumenting tool adapter layer to accept an idempotency token.
Audit & security: resume_token TTLs and HMAC keys rotate daily; logs redact token values. For Private deployments, config allows disabling resume entirely for compliance reasons.
Observability: new metrics: session_count_active, session_count_orphaned, resume_success_rate, session_eviction_rate, avg_keepalive_gap. Trace decorates spans with session_id and resume_flow boolean.
Config knobs: keepalive_window, resume_token_ttl, max_sessions_per_customer, memory_eviction_threshold, legacy_grace_window
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind runtime-keepalive-salvage for all clusters (default off)
2) Canary enable on 10% of hosted traffic with additional logging and slower TTLs
3) Run canary 72h, validate resume_success_rate and memory impact, then widen to 50%
4) Default-on after two successful cycles and removal of verbose logging
5) Announce SDK v1.2 with resume support; provide migration guide and sample code
testing_notes: Unit tests for token HMAC generation/validation and expiry edge cases
End-to-end tests simulating flaky networks with reconnects at different offsets and concurrent reconnects to ensure deterministic winner selection
Load test: 5k concurrent streaming sessions with 1% transient disconnects to measure eviction under memory pressure
Chaos test: simulate rotated HMAC keys to ensure old resume tokens are rejected cleanly and do not cause resource leak
Integration test with tool-adapter verifying idempotent replay suppression
